priya: Quick heads-up — running `terraform plan` for staging (branch: feature/sa-cleanup) and plan proposes recreating `kubernetes_service.my-app` and tainting `kubernetes_config_map.app-config`. I didn't change manifests.

alex: Can you paste the relevant plan output? especially the lines around the service and configmap.

priya: ```
Terraform will perform the following actions:
  # module.k8s.kubernetes_service.my-app will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_service" "my-app" {
+  ~ id = "k8s:default:my-app" -> (known after apply)
    # (3 unchanged attributes hidden)
  }
  # module.k8s.kubernetes_config_map.app-config must be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_config_map" "app-config" {
+  ~ data = {
+      "feature_flags" = "{...}" -> (known after apply)
    }
  }
Plan: 2 to add, 0 to change, 2 to destroy.
```

infra-bot: remote-state: backend version differs from workspace. Please run `terraform init -upgrade` if you haven't after provider bump.

emily: Two quick checks: `terraform state show module.k8s.kubernetes_service.my-app` and `terraform provider plugin list` (or `terraform providers`). Also see if provider address migrated (aws->hashicorp/aws) — that can show as replace.

priya: `terraform state show` returns "No state object found for module.k8s.kubernetes_service.my-app". But `terraform state list` shows `module.k8s.kubernetes_service.my-app[0]` present — weird.

josh: Might be an enum indexing change (count -> for_each) or provider alias change. If the provider address changed, run:
```
terraform state replace-provider \
  registry.terraform.io/old/provider registry.terraform.io/new/provider
```
Or inspect `terraform show -json` to find mismatched addresses.

alex: If state is inconsistent, safe path is `terraform state pull > state.json` and inspect the resource block, then `terraform state rm` + `terraform import` with the live resource id. Example:
```
terraform state rm module.k8s.kubernetes_service.my-app
terraform import module.k8s.kubernetes_service.my-app default/my-app
```
Do not run on prod without backup.

priya: I'll try the replace-provider first on staging. If that fails I'll import. Doing a canary apply at 11:30 PT — can someone watch the apply and rollback if it starts deleting pods? @alex @josh

emily: I'll be available 11:25-11:45 PT. Suggest adding temporary `lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["data"] }` to the configmap to avoid a disruptive replace while we sort provider migration.

priya: Update: `terraform state replace-provider` fixed the provider address mismatch for the service. The configmap still shows replace due to a default field in Helm chart change. I applied the `ignore_changes` patch in staging and ran `terraform apply` canary — service stayed, configmap was not replaced. All good.

priya: I'll open a PR to pin provider versions and add a short note in infra runbook about replace-provider procedure. Thanks all :tada:
